# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

I found two blocking scope/correctness gaps against the requested habitat/geometry deliverable and one concrete diagnostics bug in the new alkalinity budget helpers.

## Amendments

1. Blocking: this patch does not implement the requested habitat/geometry probe suite. The only new coverage is chemistry-focused work in crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:63, crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:107, crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:147, crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:205, and crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:278, and the runtime changes in crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229, crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:67, and crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:10 all support alkalinity accounting rather than the five habitat/geometry stories from the bead. There is still no probe for biofilter-media scaling, habitat-specific fouling, substrate redox/denitrification, or 1x-vs-2x equipment scaling, so the task remains functionally incomplete.
   Rationale: The bead’s primary acceptance criteria are scenario-level habitat/geometry regressions; this patch does not add them.
2. Blocking: the required habitat-specific failure diagnostics and e2e probe runner are still missing. The only added tracing is two scalar notes in crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229-239, and the new test only checks aggregate alkalinity attribution in crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:205-235. There is still no per-habitat biomass/area/modifier dump, no structured habitat/geometry trace output, and no script/runner that executes all probes and exits non-zero on envelope violations.
   Rationale: Scientific-core scenario tests are only useful if failures are diagnosable and CI can run the whole probe bundle; those deliverables are still absent.
3. Bug: the new alkalinity assertion/debug output still mislabels meq values as mg. Element::Alkalinity is explicitly documented as meq in crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:66-72, and the top-level summary switches to meq in crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:436-457, but the per-system and per-tick lines remain hard-coded to mg in crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:474-476 and crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:495-503. Any failing alkalinity assertion will therefore print internally inconsistent units and can send debugging in the wrong direction.
   Rationale: This patch is adding diagnostics; incorrect units in failure output are a real correctness problem, not a cosmetic one.
